summary: GridFS migration regression: 24/24 new tests in test_gridfs_regression.py + full backend suite 112/112 pass. Verified (a) admin image/document uploads now stream into GridFS (bucket uploads_fs) and serve via /api/uploads/{images,documents}/<file> with correct Content-Type and byte-identical bytes (SHA-256 verified); no new file appears under backend/uploads after any upload. (b) Capability PDF: GET /api/public/capability-profile returns a url that serves application/pdf from GridFS (the pre-migrated file is intact); POST /api/admin/capability-profile replaces it — old GridFS key is deleted (old URL returns 404) and new URL serves the new PDF byte-identical. (c) Client evidence lifecycle end-to-end: POST /api/client/projects/{pid}/files (multipart, scope=evidence, criterion_id) stores in GridFS at evidence/{pid}/<file>, URL serves 200 with exact bytes, DELETE removes file and URL returns 404. (d) Media list/delete lifecycle removes GridFS bytes and 404s the URL. (e) Role/auth isolation: unauthenticated POSTs to /api/admin/uploads and /api/client/projects/{pid}/files return 403; reviewer session cannot upload client files (403). Also confirmed: evidence upload is now correctly rejected with 409 when project is not editable (draft/changes_requested) — this addresses a code-review item from iteration_8. (f) Persistence: uploaded file survives `sudo supervisorctl restart backend` (GridFS-backed). (g) Migration idempotency: running scripts/migrate_local_uploads_to_gridfs twice back-to-back yields migrated=0 skipped(existing)>=1 on the second run; aggregate over uploads_fs.files shows zero duplicate filenames. (h) Regression: /api/health + /api/public/{home,services,projects,team,blogs,settings} all 200; unified /api/auth/login works for admin/client/reviewer roles; client can list/create projects; reviewer /api/reviewer/assignments returns 200.
critical_code_review_comments: backend/app/services/storage.py:save_bytes deletes then re-uploads on same key — atomic-ish but not transactional; a crash between delete and upload_from_stream would lose the file. Acceptable for admin flows but worth noting.

backend/app/api/files.py:_serve reads full file bytes into memory (open_by_key returns bytes). For large PDFs this doubles memory. Consider streaming via StreamingResponse over bucket.open_download_stream, especially since MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES defaults to 15 MB but capability PDFs can grow.

backend/scripts/migrate_local_uploads_to_gridfs.py: reads path.read_bytes() (loads entire file). Fine for the current small corpus, but if this ever runs against a large evidence archive it should stream from disk via bucket.open_upload_stream.

portal.py:upload_client_file now correctly restricts to draft/changes_requested (409 otherwise) — good. However reviewer_review_evidence still has NO editable-status guard (previously flagged in iteration_8 comment #4). A reviewer could still POST /api/reviewer/projects/{pid}/evidence/{fid}/review on a 'certified' project.

portal.py:delete_client_file has no status guard — a client whose project is 'submitted/assigned' cannot upload but CAN still delete existing evidence (401/409 not enforced here). Recommend mirroring the upload_client_file editable check.
storage.exists() is defined but never used; safe to remove or wire into upload paths to warn on hash collision.
portal.py still 913 lines (grew from 909) — split into portal_client / portal_reviewer / portal_admin (repeat comment from iterations 7, 8).
updated_files: /app/backend/tests/test_phase_bc.py (updated stale assertion — evidence upload after submit is now 409 not 200)

All uploads go through app.services.storage.save_bytes(key, bytes, ctype); serving via app/api/files.py under /api/uploads/{images|documents|certificates|evidence/{pid}}/<file>. rca of the issue: Two initial test-script issues surfaced and were self-fixed: (1) reviewer list endpoint path was /api/reviewer/assignments not /api/reviewer/projects — corrected. (2) capability-replace test ran before migration-idempotency test and deleted the migrated GridFS entry (while its disk copy was intentionally kept), causing the migration script to re-migrate — fixed by making the idempotency test run the script twice back-to-back and asserting the SECOND run is a no-op. One pre-existing test (test_phase_bc.py::test_upload_serve_delete_and_reviewer_review) failed because the main agent tightened upload_client_file to reject uploads on non-editable projects (409) — the assertion was stale from iteration_8 (that iteration explicitly flagged this as a code-review action item that has now been implemented). Stale assertion updated to expect 409. No product bugs found.
